title: Add an actionable Japanese uninstall procedure
outOfScope: Changing uninstall runtime behavior, deletion semantics, installer payloads, or Make targets.
Claiming that AI Cockpit independently provides identity, isolation, immutable audit, or enterprise compliance.
Adding a version-pinned installation or uninstall path.
Treating disable mode as uninstall or allowing purge without separate destructive confirmation and evidence export.
General three-language documentation alignment, deprecated-asset cleanup, release publication, or final plan cleanup.

sources.reason: JA-DOC-001 records the release-blocking absence of an actionable Japanese uninstall procedure.
Lifecycle reference whose implemented proposal/state-output behavior must be separated from required but non-installed detached removal and purge designs.
Current-state authority whose governed update/uninstall row must distinguish installed proposal behavior from non-installed model-only removal and purge code.
Implemented read-only proposal behavior and mode semantics that the Japanese guide must describe accurately.
Implemented confirmation, detached, drift, ownership, receipt, and runtime-removal verification boundaries.
Installed repository exposes ai-cockpit-uninstall-propose as the supported proposal entrypoint.
Complete prompt-first Japanese beginner route where uninstall and recovery must be actionable.
WI-16 requires every Japanese assessment blocker to complete a separate corrective lifecycle before documentation alignment.

riskAssessment.reason: Incorrect or shallow uninstall guidance can cause evidence loss, confuse disable with removal, or let the Japanese release assessment pass without an executable beginner path.

executionDecision.reason: The user made Japanese capability mandatory, authorized correction of every finding, and directed continuous execution before documentation alignment and release.

preReviewWarnings: The guide must not imply that generating a proposal deletes files.
The default path preserves evidence; purge remains separately destructive and cannot be silently selected.
The assessment must require an actionable structure, not a Japanese uninstall keyword.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: A1: The Japanese beginner installation guide contains a complete prompt-first uninstall route covering read-only facts, disable/preserve-evidence/purge choices, exact proposal review, explicit bounded confirmation, detached execution, receipt verification, STOP conditions, and recovery.

A2: Every step explains purpose, expected PASS, STOP condition, and responsible owner in language usable by a person with no programming experience; commands are delegated to the agent unless a real installed entrypoint must be shown and explained.
A3: The guide is version-neutral and dynamically uses the repository's installed release behavior without a hardcoded semantic version.

A4: The default preserve-evidence path retains bootstrap, archive, human decisions, project policy, complexity baseline, audit evidence, and project-owned files; modified, unknown-owned, or drifted paths remain untouched.

A5: Disable is distinguished from uninstall, purge requires evidence export plus a separate destructive review and confirmation, and proposal generation writes only its reviewable output JSON without Runtime or deletion writes.
A6: Japanese upgrade and troubleshooting pages route readers to the same actionable uninstall and recovery procedure without duplicating divergent semantics.
A7: The Japanese capability assessor and documentation checker require stable actionable markers and semantic boundaries; keyword-only, missing-step, missing-STOP, or missing-evidence mutations fail.

A8: The installed lifecycle reference and Capability Truth Matrix state that proposal/state output files are the only current public writes, uninstall facts have no public builder, proposal identity has no digest binding, and detached/purge filesystem execution is template-only model code absent from the installed payload.

A9: A regenerated assessment reports JA-DOC-001 pass with source, test, command, limitation, and digest evidence, while separately blocking JA-UNINSTALL-RUNTIME-001 because the current detached executor is a non-installed in-memory model rather than a public filesystem-removal entrypoint; general Japanese fluency remains a non-claim.

A10: The plan, Contract, implementation, tests, assessment, and acceptance evidence are bidirectionally mapped, then full finish/archive, one PR, Hosted CI, merge, ai-close-work-item, branch cleanup, and synchronized main complete before the separate installed-detached-uninstaller-runtime corrective starts.
guidelines: Use production proposal/state-output code and installed catalog evidence; treat detached removal and purge as non-installed models and do not invent a public deletion command.
Prefer copy-ready Japanese prompts and human checkpoints over unexplained command lines.
Preserve fail-closed drift, ownership, evidence-export, detached-execution, receipt, and runtime-removal verification boundaries.
Keep installation and uninstall guidance version-neutral.
Strengthen machine checks so document presence or a keyword cannot clear JA-DOC-001.
Record instruction → plan → implementation → acceptance evidence in both the human plan and machine traceability registry.

intent.problem: The Japanese capability report correctly blocks release because Japanese engineers have no actionable uninstall procedure. Worse, the current assessor clears JA-DOC-001 when any one of three documents contains only the word uninstall, so a non-actionable edit could falsely authorize release. Implementation review also proved that the installed repository exposes only a proposal/state-output surface; detached removal and purge are non-installed in-memory models without filesystem behavior.
constraints: Do not change runtime deletion behavior or expose an unimplemented public executor command.
Keep proposal generation free of Runtime/deletion writes, identify its output JSON write, and require a separate confirmation before detached execution.
Preserve evidence by default and leave project-owned, modified, drifted, and unknown-owned paths untouched.
Keep purge separately destructive and confirmation-gated.
Write for a person with no programming experience and avoid fixed release versions.
Record the missing public executor as a separate blocking corrective and complete both lifecycles before broader documentation alignment.
intent.rationale: A prompt-first Japanese procedure bound to the actual implemented boundary, plus mutation-resistant structural checks, closes the documentation gap without inventing deletion capability. A separate stable runtime finding keeps release blocked until a real public detached executor exists.

rawUserRequest: Japanese capability is mandatory for adopter engineers. Correct every Japanese assessment issue before release. The installation path must be simple and detailed enough for a person with no programming experience, use prompts where possible, avoid fixed versions, preserve evidence, record discovered process problems, and complete the full PR, merge, closure, and branch-cleanup lifecycle before continuing.

authorityEvidence.scope: Correct JA-DOC-001, strengthen the process against omission, and complete its governed lifecycle before later phases.
